lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 9: ConfigMaps and Secrets
lesson.description: Inject settings into Pods as variables and files, see which ones update live, learn why a Secret is only base64-encoded, and lock a ConfigMap as immutable.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Keep settings out of images. Variables are read once at start; mounted files update. A Secret is base64, so guard who can read it.

steps.title: The four rules in the recap

items.what: ConfigMaps and Secrets keep settings out of images. Containers read them as variables or files.
Variables are fixed when the container starts. Volume files update after a delay. `subPath` files never do.
A Secret is base64-encoded and, by default, unencrypted in etcd. Limit who can read Secrets and who can create Pods.
`immutable: true` turns every change into a new, named version you can roll out and roll back.

commands.note: add `--dry-run=client -o yaml` to see the object
the key is the file name

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero` as your context namespace. The lesson does not print a cluster name. A Pod and its ConfigMap or Secret must be in the same namespace. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Which ways of injecting a setting update a running container, and which stay fixed?
exercises.a: Variables are fixed when the container starts. Volume files update after about a minute. A `subPath` mount never updates in a running Pod.

exercises.q: What is a Secret on the API, and what is it not?
exercises.a: It is base64-encoded. By default it is unencrypted in etcd. base64 is not encryption. Limit who can read Secrets and who can create Pods.

exercises.q: What does `immutable: true` force you to do when a value must change?
exercises.a: Create a new object under a new name and point the workload at it. The symptom of editing an immutable object is `field is immutable when immutable is set`.

exercises.q: What is the size limit, and what happens if the Pod and the ConfigMap are in different namespaces?
exercises.a: 1 MiB per ConfigMap or Secret. Use volumes for more. A reference in another namespace gives `CreateContainerConfigError`.

exercises.q: Create a Secret with `--from-literal` and read `.data.password` through jsonpath and `base64 -d`. What do you get back?
exercises.a: The original literal. Kubernetes encoded it. The cheat sheet says to let Kubernetes encode it, using `stringData` or `--from-literal`.

exercises.q: Change a ConfigMap that a Deployment reads as an environment variable. The app still shows the old value. What command does the lesson give?
exercises.a: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/app`. New Pods read the new values. The running container already took its variables at start.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A Pod stays in `CreateContainerConfigError` and describe ends with `configmap "app-confg" not found`. What caused it in the lesson, and what retries?
exercises.a: A typo in `configMapKeyRef.name`. Fix the name, or create the object. The kubelet retries on its own. Mark a reference `optional: true` only when the app can run without it.

exercises.q: Logins fail with a password that looks right. How did the lesson say the newline got into `data`?
exercises.a: The value was encoded with `echo` instead of `echo -n`, so `data` holds `password` plus a newline. Use `stringData` or `kubectl create secret --from-literal`.

exercises.q: A Secret value is in Git or in `last-applied-configuration`. What do you do first?
exercises.a: Rotate the credential first, then clean up. Removing the file does not remove it from history.
